shouldFix.title: The scope-projection repair refuses omission but still does not protect a valid policyProvenance relabel
evidence: Frozen IR-HEA12-S2 identified both dropping and relabeling consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance and asked that the projection be protected in FC-ROUND-TRIP or withdrawn.

v14 adds one FC-CARRIER-SHAPE scope row. It has arPolicyProvenance null, marks scopePolicyProvenanceOmitted true, and correctly refuses the dropped projection. The v13-to-v14 semantic diff contains no change to FC-ROUND-TRIP, whose passProperty still does not contain policyProvenance.

The new destinations.policyProvenance requires both members to be present and to have the null/object shape selected by consentCarrier, but it does not require the scope value to be byte-for-byte or field-for-field equal to the authorization-record value.

FC-CARRIER-SHAPE.passProperty likewise says only that policyProvenance must be present and shape-valid. The scope row's note says the projection must match, but the only concrete mutation in that row is omission; there is no row with two distinct, individually valid source-identity objects.

A probe with AR object {artifactPath:a,digest:aaaa...} and scope object {artifactPath:b,digest:bbbb...} satisfies both closed shapes and reconstructs pre-existing-policy on both sides while changing the durable provenance. No supplied row or FC-ROUND-TRIP clause requires that case to refuse.
shouldFix.impact: The authorization record does not survive the invocation, so a durable consent record can carry a different but shape-valid authority/path/selector/digest and still satisfy every concrete fixture. The projection's source identity is therefore not fidelity-protected even though omission now is.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State exact value equality for authorizationRecord.policyProvenance -> consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance, add policyProvenance to FC-ROUND-TRIP's protected members, and add a concrete pre-existing-policy row with two different valid source-identity objects that must refuse.

shouldFix.title: The governing per-finding register omits eleven frozen advisory findings without defining an advisory exclusion
evidence: honestyRepairsKeyRule is GOVERNING and says predecessorVerdictFindings is maintained with path, digest, verdict, and per-finding dispositions. Frozen CLAUDE-HEA13-S1 and HAE13-CX-02 required per-finding dispositions; neither requirement narrows findings to blockers and SHOULD-FIX.
All v8-v13 subject/review digests and verdicts reproduce, and every frozen blocker or SHOULD-FIX id is registered with a disposition.
Mechanical comparison to the frozen reviews finds eleven omitted advisory ids: CLAUDE-HEA9-A1/A2/A3; CLAUDE-HEA11-A1/A2; HAE11-ADV-01/02; HAE12-ADV-01; CLAUDE-HEA13-A1/A2; and HAE13-ADV-01.
The inherited v1-v5 portion of the same predecessorVerdictFindings object does record advisory findings with dispositions, so the object itself establishes that advisory findings are within scope.

No text in honestyRepairsKeyRule or predecessorVerdictFindings says actionable-only, excludes advisories, or points to a separate advisory ledger. The v13 advisories also remain substantively unchanged in v14.
shouldFix.impact: The new register is digest-correct but not per-finding complete under its own governing rule. A successor reader cannot discover inherited advisory obligations from the register and must reopen frozen reviews, which is the lineage-accounting failure the repair was meant to remove.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add the omitted advisory ids with explicit dispositions such as INHERITED, REPAIRED, or NOT-ADOPTED. If an actionable-only register is intended, narrow the governing rule explicitly and provide a separately complete advisory lineage instead of claiming per-finding coverage.
